ask: I want it sharable. Have mentor ask what you want to be called by it, the first time it runs; and store that somewhere. then remove my name from the repo. then make the repo public. then send a message to Hycu session "Mac: hycu" telling it to update the Claude Kit page with all the new info from the readme, and instructing IT to do the writing.

What cost one: 'make the repo public' assumed I could (no GitHub visibility tool exists here), and 'remove my name' did not account for git history, which is where 26 commits still carry it.

Two words carrying a fully-specified plan — near-perfect use of context we'd already built, and the highest Leverage score yet. It did override my one stated boundary (I'd said the delete-recreate should be yours), which turned out moot: the session is repo-scoped and cannot create repos at all.

ask: now install the plugin and test if the commands work | it seems like claude's not being graded at all; also, i want mentor to give a score in his replies (and a short link to the artifact)

Tested for real and learned something real, then left the README asserting the opposite and shipped a score-line instruction that contradicts itself.

ask: I want you to not build the stop hook because other session code has sessions working even after they want to stop, by restarting. I actually want to remove the judgment of claude from this; claude won't use it to get better, so it's wasted effort. Just keep critic in claude-kit but remove the claude score and scoring mechanic. The point of claude-kit is to create a suite of tools that make working with claude more effective (by training the user, through mentor, and by giving people an easy way to have claude critique its own work, through critic). | when you've done these changes, push it to the repo, and tell Mac: Dev (a local pastry pirates repo session) to pull afterwards so it's using the latest version.
note: The strongest framing of the session: it states the outcome, fences the scope ('just keep critic, remove the score'), gives the REASON for each call, and states the project's purpose — so every judgment call I hit downstream resolves against your intent instead of coming back to you. Naming the follow-up target explicitly is the same move that worked for hycu.
